🎯 Cache Hit Methodology — Prometheus Cache Calculations

📖 What this chart showsSeparates the four ways cache hit rate can be measured and explains the gap between benchmark tool output and gauge averages.

What you are looking at: A table with four rows — token-weighted, gauge-active-average, gauge-timeline-average, and gauge-peak — each with its value and interpretation.

The four methods: • Token-weighted: Δ(cached_tokens) / (Δcached + Δcompute). Matches bench_serving output exactly. • Gauge active avg: mean of non-zero sglang_cache_hit_rate samples. Filters out idle windows. • Gauge timeline avg: mean over ALL samples including idle — almost always misleadingly low. • Gauge peak: maximum instantaneous gauge value.

In the reference run: token-weighted 34 % vs gauge-active 59 %. The gap means even during active windows, a large share of tokens still go through prefill_compute — likely unique prompt suffixes beyond the shared prefix.

What to do: If token-weighted << gauge-active, inspect prompt structure. Adding a shared system-prompt prefix that all requests use dramatically raises the token-weighted hit rate.

This section separates the reader-facing cache-hit KPI from diagnostics. The primary KPI is cache-served prompt/prefill tokens divided by total cache-served + compute-served prompt/prefill tokens. AMOprof uses the same shared cache-hit function in Executive, Interactive, and End Report; gauges and cached/prompt counters are shown only as diagnostics because their denominator semantics can diverge across SGLang versions/export paths.
CalculationValueHow to interpret
Primary cache hit0.00%Benchmark-comparable prompt/prefill work-avoidance KPI: cache-served tokens / (cache-served + compute-served tokens). Method: unavailable.
Effective prompt counter diagnostic0.00%(Δsglang_cached_tokens_total + Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"}) / (Δsglang_cached_tokens_total + Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"} + Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_compute"}).
Cached/prompt diagnostic0.00%Δsglang_cached_tokens_total / Δsglang_prompt_tokens_total × 100. Diagnostic only; prompt_tokens_total may represent total prompt tokens rather than uncached prefill work.
Time weighted0.00%avg_over_time(sglang_cache_hit_rate[window]) × 100 over the selected report window. Diagnostic only because the gauge can be overwritten frequently.
Request weighted0.00%sum(rate(sglang_request_cache_hit_total[window])) / sum(rate(sglang_request_total[window])) × 100 where those counters are exported.
Prefill-token cache hit0.00%Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"} / (Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"} + Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_compute"}). Prometheus equivalent when request/response JSON is unavailable.
Gauge active average0.00%Mean of non-zero sglang_cache_hit_rate samples. Active windows: 0 / 0.
Gauge timeline average0.00%Mean across all collected gauge samples, including idle/dead-space intervals.
Gauge peak0.00%Maximum observed instantaneous/rolling cache-hit gauge value.
📐 Formula
Primary cache hit = cache-served prompt/prefill tokens / (cache-served prompt/prefill tokens + compute-served prompt/prefill tokens) × 100 Request JSON exact = Σmeta_info.cached_tokens / Σ(meta_info.cached_tokens + meta_info.prompt_tokens) × 100 OpenAI usage exact = Σusage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens / Σusage.prompt_tokens × 100 Prometheus fallback = Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"} / (Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"} + Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_compute"}) × 100 Effective prompt counter diagnostic = (Δsglang_cached_tokens_total + Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"}) / (Δsglang_cached_tokens_total + Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"} + Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_compute"}) × 100 Gauge active average = avg(sglang_cache_hit_rate samples where value > 0) × 100 Gauge timeline average = avg(all sglang_cache_hit_rate samples) × 100 Gauge peak = max(sglang_cache_hit_rate samples) × 100 Cached/prompt diagnostic = Δsglang_cached_tokens_total / Δsglang_prompt_tokens_total × 100 Calculation method used for main KPI: unavailable

📊 P50 / P90 / P99 Summary

📖 What this chart showsPer-request latency percentiles (TTFT, ITL, E2E) from Prometheus histogram_quantile() — the truest view of tail latency.

What you are looking at: Three rows of bar charts — one for TTFT (Time to First Token), one for ITL/TPOT (inter-token / decode step latency), one for E2E (full request wall-clock time). Each row has four bars: Mean, P50, P90, P99.

How to read the numbers: A healthy inference server has a flat P50→P99 ratio (less than 2×). A wide P90→P99 spread means occasional cold-cache prefills or queue contention spikes. A high TTFT (>500 ms) with moderate ITL indicates the bottleneck is in the KV cache load path (L2/L3 (AI Memory Node / remote storage) miss), not in compute. A high ITL (>100 ms) means the GPU is memory-bandwidth-bound during decode — HBM is likely saturated.

For KV$: P99 TTFT is the most sensitive indicator of L3 (AI Memory Node / remote storage) cache misses. An L1 hit gives near-zero TTFT; an L3 (AI Memory Node / remote storage) hit adds 50–200 ms just for loading KV blocks from NVMe. If P99 >> P50 on TTFT, check the KV eviction/load-back charts — the working set is larger than your HBM pool.

What to do: P99 TTFT driven by long contexts → enable `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`. Driven by cold cache → increase DRAM/NVMe tier capacity.

📐 Formula & Metrics Used
📊 SGLang Prometheus histogram bucket metrics
TTFT P50/P90/P99 = histogram_quantile(0.50/0.90/0.99, rate(sglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket[window])) × 1000 ITL P50/P90/P99 = histogram_quantile(0.50/0.90/0.99, rate(sglang_inter_token_latency_seconds_bucket[window])) × 1000 E2E P50/P90/P99 = histogram_quantile(0.50/0.90/0.99, rate(sglang_e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket[window])) × 1000 Prompt token percentiles = histogram_quantile(..., rate(sglang_prompt_tokens_histogram_bucket[window])) or histogram_quantile(..., rate(sglang_prompt_tokens_bucket[window])) Output token percentiles = histogram_quantile(..., rate(sglang_generation_tokens_histogram_bucket[window])) or histogram_quantile(..., rate(sglang_generation_tokens_bucket[window])) Fallback when token histogram buckets are absent = per-request counter delta / request count, shown as a flat conservative distribution.
Percentile charts are tail/shape diagnostics. They are not used as the mean TTFT/ITL/E2E KPI tiles.

⚡ AI Operation Phase Analysis — Prefill (TTFT) vs Decode (TPOT)

📖 What this chart showsSide-by-side Prefill (TTFT) and Decode (TPOT) panels with severity badges, statistics, and a token composition bar.

What you are looking at: Left panel = Prefill: TTFT in ms, context tokens split into compute vs cached, and a phase-driver diagnosis. Right panel = Decode: TPOT in ms/token, total decode tokens, peak throughput. Below: a token composition bar — cyan (cached) | orange (compute) | green (decode).

How to read the badges: TTFT > 1000 ms → HIGH (long context or cold cache). TPOT > 80 ms/tok → HIGH (HBM-bandwidth-bound). A run with TTFT=33 s and TPOT=2.3 s is dominated by long-context prefill: 43M-token prompts hit every KV block in the cache and still run compute for uncached tails.

For KV$: The cyan fraction of the token bar is your effective KV$ reuse rate. Sub-30 % cyan means less than a third of prompt tokens were served without compute — the KV pool is too small for the working set or the workload has too little prefix repetition.

What to do: TTFT too high with large compute segment → chunked prefill or KV quantisation. TPOT too high → speculative decoding or reduce concurrent batch size to keep more KV in HBM.

📐 Formula & Metrics Used
📊 sglang_summary.json derived from SGLang Prometheus counters
Mean TTFT ms = Δsglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_sum / Δsglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_count × 1000 P50 TTFT ms = histogram_quantile(0.50, rate(sglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket[window])) × 1000 Mean TPOT/ITL ms = Δsglang_inter_token_latency_seconds_sum / Δsglang_inter_token_latency_seconds_count × 1000 P50 TPOT/ITL ms = histogram_quantile(0.50, rate(sglang_inter_token_latency_seconds_bucket[window])) × 1000 Mean E2E ms = Δsglang_e2e_request_latency_seconds_sum / Δsglang_e2e_request_latency_seconds_count × 1000 Prefill cached tokens = Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_cache"} Prefill compute tokens = Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="prefill_compute"} Decode tokens = Δsglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode="decode"} or Δsglang_generation_tokens_total Decode throughput = active_mean(sglang_gen_throughput) or Δsglang_generation_tokens_total / Δtime_sec
Mean tiles use request-weighted counter deltas. Percentiles are shown separately in the P50/P90/P99 section.

⏱ GPU Utilisation, Power & HBM Timeline

📖 What this chart showsPer-GPU time series of SM utilisation, HBM occupancy, power draw, and HBM bandwidth active fraction from DCGM.

What you are looking at: A 4-panel chart (or 2×2 grid): (1) GPU Util % — DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL (SM occupancy). (2) HBM Used (GB) — DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED. (3) Power (W) — DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE. (4) HBM BW Active % — DCGM_FI_PROF_DRAM_ACTIVE × 100.

Important: GPU util is SM occupancy, not HBM bandwidth. An A100 can show 100 % util at low HBM BW (compute-bound attention) or 40 % util at full HBM BW (decode, memory-bandwidth-bound). The HBM BW Active panel is the direct bandwidth saturation signal.

In the reference run: mean 96.4 % util, peak 100 %, HBM 89 % full (35.7/40 GB), power 392 W/GPU. The GPUs are fully loaded during a combined long-context prefill (compute-bound) and decode (bandwidth-bound) workload.

For KV$: HBM fill % is the L1 tier gauge. Pinned at 89–100 % means every new session competes for KV space. Sudden drop in HBM fill followed by a load_back spike = session evicted, then immediately requested again — classic thrashing.

What to do: Util > 95 % with HBM > 85 % and rising TPOT → KV quantisation (FP8) to free HBM and improve batching.

Static PNG fallback / print view
📐 Formula & Metrics Used
📊 gpu_timeseries.csv — nvidia-smi (1s) + DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL + DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED + DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE
GPU util % : DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL (Prometheus) OR nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits HBM used (GB) : DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED / 1024 (MiB → GB) HBM util % : FB_USED / FB_TOTAL × 100 FB_TOTAL = DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED + DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE GPU power (W) : DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE (Prometheus) OR nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw --format=csv,noheader,nounits Timeseries step : 1s (nvidia-smi) or 15s (Prometheus query_range) Static panels : GPU util %, total GPU power W, HBM used GB/GPU End Report and Interactive use the same gpu_timeseries.csv rows and the same active-GPU display rule; completely idle/all-zero devices are hidden from the visual mean when active GPUs exist. HBM uses visible per-GPU traces + mean when FB_USED is present
GPU util reflects SM occupancy, not memory bandwidth. A100 can show 100% util at low HBM BW during compute-bound attention. Power includes idle base draw (~50W/GPU); inference active draw typically 250–400W/GPU on A100.
No data for Inference Metrics
📐 Formula & Metrics Used
📊 sglang_timeseries.csv — SGLang Prometheus /metrics endpoint, 1s scrape
TTFT (ms) : sglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_sum / sglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_count × 1000 (Δ over scrape window = per-interval mean) TPOT / ITL (ms) : sglang_inter_token_latency_seconds_sum / sglang_inter_token_latency_seconds_count × 1000 Gen throughput : sglang_gen_throughput[engine_type=unified] (tokens/s, real-time) Cache hit rate : sglang_cache_hit_rate[engine_type=unified] (0–1, rolling) Token usage : sglang_full_token_usage (fraction of L1 KV pool occupied) OR sglang_token_usage (older SGLang versions) num_running_reqs: sglang_num_running_reqs[engine_type=unified] (active sessions) num_queue_reqs : sglang_num_queue_reqs (sessions waiting for capacity)
TTFT includes prefill attention compute + KV cache lookup. TPOT (inter-token latency) is the decode step time — dominated by HBM memory bandwidth. gen_throughput is a rolling 1s window reported by SGLang, not derived. All metrics are Prometheus counters (cumulative); rates are computed as Δ(sum)/Δ(count) per scrape interval.

💾 Memory Profile — HBM, DRAM & KV Cache

📖 What this chart showsCombined time series of HBM (GPU), DRAM (host), and KV cache tier usage — the full three-tier memory picture on one canvas.

What you are looking at: Overlapping time series for: • HBM Used (GB) and HBM util % per GPU (DCGM). • Estimated HBM BW (GB/s) derived from TPOT × model size. • DRAM BW (GB/s) from AMDuProf (when available). • KV pool usage — sglang_full_token_usage fraction. • hicache host tokens (L2 DRAM tier occupancy).

How to read: HBM flat near 100 % + rising hicache host tokens = runtime is actively spilling KV to DRAM (L1→L2). That + rising NVMe write activity = spillover reaching L3 (DRAM→NVMe). DRAM BW spike during HBM saturation confirms active L1→L2 DMA.

In the reference run: HBM 89 %, 8 GPUs × 17.5 GB weights = 22 GB/GPU left for KV. At 327 KB/token, this allows ~67K tokens in HBM before spilling — any 131K-token context immediately uses both HBM and DRAM tiers.

For KV$: This is the single best chart for seeing tier spillover in action. A rising hicache_host line concurrent with flat/full HBM is the L1→L2 spill event.

What to do: HBM pinned at 100 % → KV quantisation (FP8 halves per-token cost) or reduce `--max-num-seqs`.

📐 Formula & Metrics Used
📊 gpu_timeseries.csv (HBM) + amduprof_pcm_raw.csv (DRAM) + sglang_timeseries.csv (KV pool)
HBM used (GB) : DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED / 1024 per GPU HBM util % : FB_USED / 15360 (A100) × 100 HBM BW est (GB/s) : model_params_GB_per_GPU / (TPOT_ms / 1000) = (n_params × 2 / n_gpus) / tpot_s [assumes FP16 weights] Accurate ONLY during pure steady-state decode (TPOT 20–200 ms). Long-context / prefill-heavy runs produce misleadingly low values — see caveat banner. DRAM BW (GB/s) : amduprof_pcm_raw.csv → "Total Mem Bw (GB/s)" = DDR4/5 read+write transactions × 64B / interval Peak: 204.8 GB/s (default (unrecognised CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8259CL CPU @ 2.50GHz)) DRAM util % : total_BW / 204.8 × 100 DRAM used GB : SGLang L2 HiCache residency when available = sglang_hicache_host_used_tokens × KV_bytes_per_token / 1024^3 bounded by configured L2/HiCache capacity (23200 GB) Raw OS DRAM timeseries is not used when it exceeds the L2 allocation. KV pool usage : sglang_full_token_usage × max_total_num_tokens × kv_bytes_per_token / 1e9 [GB] KV active tokens : sglang_hicache_host_used_tokens (L2 DRAM) sglang_kv_used_tokens (L1 HBM, if available)
HBM BW estimation from TPOT is accurate ±10% during decode-dominated phases. For prefill-heavy workloads use DCGM_FI_PROF_DRAM_ACTIVE which measures actual HBM transactions. DRAM BW includes all NUMA traffic, while the DRAM-used chart intentionally reports the configured L2 HiCache residency/capacity rather than whole-host OS memory when those differ.

🗃 KV Cache Footprint & HBM Capacity Analysis

📖 What this chart showsStatic KV cache capacity analysis: bytes/token, max HBM context, weight footprint, quantisation savings, and spill threshold.

What you are looking at: Six mini-cards showing: • KV Bytes/Token: 2 × n_layers × n_kv_heads × head_dim × dtype_bytes. • Max Context (HBM): tokens fitting in HBM KV pool. • Weight Footprint: GB of HBM used by model parameters. • KV Pool Used %: fraction of pre-allocated pool occupied. • INT8 Savings: doubled token capacity at INT8. • Spill Threshold: token count that triggers DRAM spill.

For DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B in BF16 on A100 40 GB: 2 × 80 layers × 8 KV-heads × 128 dim × 2 bytes = 327 KB/token ~17.5 GB weights/GPU → ~22.5 GB left for KV → ~68K tokens max At 131K context window: every request immediately overflows HBM INT8 KV doubles capacity to ~137K before spilling.

For KV$: The Spill Threshold card directly tells you the context length at which you START generating NVMe traffic. Any prompt longer than this will hit L2/L3 (AI Memory Node / remote storage).

What to do: Contexts regularly exceeding spill threshold → enable FP8 KV (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2` in SGLang ≥0.4). Accuracy impact is typically <0.5 % on standard benchmarks.

The KV (Key-Value) cache stores attention tensors for every token in the context window. Per-token cost is fixed by model architecture and runtime dtype. It sets the maximum context length, batch size ceiling, and the point at which hicache DRAM spill begins.

📐 Formula & Derivation
📊 Derived from model architecture DB + runtime dtype
GQA/MHA: 2 × n_layers × n_kv_heads × head_dim × dtype_bytes = 2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 327,680 bytes = 320 KB per token HBM pool = 15 GB total - 0.3 GB weights - 0.5 GB runtime = 14.2 GB Max tokens = 14.2 GB / 320 KB = 43,334 tokens INT8 (1B): 163,840 bytes/tok → 86,668 max tokens (2×) FP8 (1B): 163,840 bytes/tok → 86,668 max tokens (2×) INT4 (0.5B): 81,920 bytes/tok → 173,336 max tokens (4×)
Architecture matched from built-in DB on model name. dtype from sglang_summary.json kv_cache_dtype (default FP16). KV is replicated across all tensor-parallel GPUs — the limit applies to the whole 8-GPU system, not per GPU.
KV blocks are the management unit of the KV cache (16 tokens = 0.0 MB each for this model). Offload = blocks moving L1 HBM → L2 DRAM hicache. Eviction = blocks removed from L2 when pool is full. Lifetime = estimated duration a block survives before eviction.

📐 Formula & Metrics Used
📊 sglang_timeseries.csv + model arch DB
Block size tokens : SGLang default = 16 tokens/block Block size MB : block_tokens x kv_bytes_per_token / 1024^2 = 0.00 MB L1 pool blocks : sglang_max_total_num_tokens / 16 = 0 L2 pool blocks : sglang_hicache_host_total_tokens / 16 = 0 Offload rate : Δ(hicache_host_used_tokens) / 16 / run_duration_s = 0.0000 blk/s Eviction rate : offload_rate x (l2_fill - 0.8) / 0.2 [when l2_fill > 80%] Block lifetime : l2_pool_blocks / offload_rate = 0s
hicache_host_used_tokens from sglang_hicache_host_used_tokens[engine_type=unified]. L3.5 (AI Memory Node / remote storage) activity is shown only when backuped_tokens_total or prefetched_tokens_total has a positive delta, or when a mapped local block trace exists. load_back-only (L2→L1 restore) and evicted-only counters are treated as ambiguous/cache-pressure signals and are not counted as L3.5 (AI Memory Node / remote storage) usage. True per-block event logs require SGLang debug logging or blktrace.
KV cache reads happen on every prefill step. The latency cost per token depends on which tier holds it: L1 HBM is fast (~0.16ms/token), L2 DRAM hicache is 10× slower, and L3 KV offload is ~570× slower. This section shows the actual tier distribution for this run and the TTFT impact if tokens had been served from each tier.

📐 Formula & Derivation — Tier Read Latency
📊 Derived: kv_bytes_per_token (model arch) + tier bandwidth constants + SGLang metrics
KV read latency per token = kv_bytes_per_token / tier_bandwidth L1 HBM : 327,680 bytes / (2000 GB/s × 10⁹) = 0.0002 ms/token L2 DRAM : 327,680 bytes / (200.0 GB/s × 10⁹) = 0.0016 ms/token L3 : 327,680 bytes / (3.5 GB/s × 10⁹) = 0.09 ms/token Total KV read cost for 0 cached tokens: From L1 : 0 × 0.0002 ms = 0 ms From L2 : 0 × 0.0016 ms = 0 ms From L3 : 0 × 0.09 ms = 0 s Weighted latency = (L1_tokens×L1_lat + L2_tokens×L2_lat + L3_tokens×L3_lat) / (L1_tokens + L2_tokens + L3_tokens) = 0.0000 ms/token Bandwidth constants: L1 HBM = 2000 GB/s (A100 HBM2e spec) L2 DRAM = 200.0 GB/s (measured via AMDuProf, or 205 GB/s peak — default (unrecognised CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8259CL CPU @ 2.50GHz)) L3 = 3.5 GB/s (sequential read, /dev/nvme0n1 spec)
Token tier counts sourced from SGLang: max_total_num_tokens (L1 cap), full_token_usage×cap (L1 used), hicache_host_used/total_tokens (L2), kv_l3_storage_tokens (L3). L2 BW overridden by live AMDuProf measurement when available.

⏳ Latency Breakdown & Token Composition

📖 What this chart showsDecomposes end-to-end request latency into queue time, prefill (TTFT), and decode (N × ITL) — plus a token-composition bar.

What you are looking at: A stacked bar where each segment represents one phase: queue_time | TTFT | decode_total. Alongside it, a proportional token bar shows prefill_cached | prefill_compute | decode_output fractions.

How to read: Large prefill_compute segment + TTFT dominating the latency bar → cache hit rate is low (KV eviction pressure or diverse prompts). decode_total dominating → model is HBM-bandwidth-bound; every decode step re-reads full model weights from HBM. queue_time dominating → insufficient capacity; requests are waiting before any GPU work starts.

For KV$: The token bar's cyan (prefill_cached) fraction is the most direct measure of KV$ effectiveness. Aim for >70 % cached on workloads with repeated system prompts. Sub-30 % signals either an undersized HBM pool or a workload with no shared prefix structure.

What to do: Low cached → check HBM fill % and eviction rate. High queue → scale batch size or add replicas.

📐 Formula & Metrics Used
📊 SGLang Prometheus counters and token composition counters
Mean TTFT ms = Δsglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_sum / Δsglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_count × 1000 Mean ITL/TPOT ms = Δsglang_inter_token_latency_seconds_sum / Δsglang_inter_token_latency_seconds_count × 1000 Mean E2E ms = Δsglang_e2e_request_latency_seconds_sum / Δsglang_e2e_request_latency_seconds_count × 1000 Prompt tokens/request = Δsglang_prompt_tokens_total / Δsglang_num_requests_total Output tokens/request = Δsglang_generation_tokens_total / Δsglang_num_requests_total Cache diagnostics = sglang_cache_hit_rate and sglang_realtime_tokens_total{mode=...}

🔄 Session / Stream Analysis

📖 What this chart showsPer-inference-session breakdown: concurrency, KV footprint, and I/O bandwidth consumed by each active request.

What you are looking at: Four panels: (1) Gantt bars: session start/end times. (2) KV footprint: peak tokens in cache per session. (3) BW consumed: NVMe MB/s attributed per session (biosnoop). (4) Concurrency: simultaneous active sessions over time.

How to read: Uniform session lengths + similar KV footprints = predictable, easy-to-size workload. A few outliers with 10× KV footprint of peers = long-context requests monopolising resources and pushing shorter sessions' KV out of HBM, degrading everyone's cache hit rate.

For KV$: Sessions whose context exceeds HBM capacity generate continuous L2/L3 (AI Memory Node / remote storage) traffic on every decode step. A 200K-token session with a 68K-token L1 capacity has a permanent 132K-token 'hot tail' in L2/L3 (AI Memory Node / remote storage) that gets paged in/out continuously.

What to do: Route outlier long-context sessions to a dedicated server, or enable sliding window attention to cap the active KV footprint.

📊 Combined: node_exporter + SGLang Prometheus + DCGM
§88 L3 read per output token: ssd_read_per_output_token = rate(node_disk_read_bytes_total[W]) / rate(sglang_generation_tokens_total[W]) §89 L3 write per input token: ssd_write_per_input_token = rate(node_disk_written_bytes_total[W]) / rate(sglang_prompt_tokens_total[W]) §93 Throughput capacity context: max_tokens_from_l3 = l3_read_bw / kv_bytes_per_token capacity_context = compare(gpu_token_rate, max_tokens_from_l3) gpu_token_rate = sglang_gen_throughput peak [tok/s] l3_read_bw = node_disk_read_bytes_total rate OR rd_total_bytes/run_duration §90/91 Correlation (offload vs SSD write, onboard vs SSD read): corr(sglang_backuped_tokens × kv_bytes, node_disk_written_bytes) corr(sglang_prefetched_tokens × kv_bytes, node_disk_read_bytes) # do not use load_back_tokens as SSD/L3 bytes Seasonal period: FFT on R(t) = binned read bytes/sec timeseries dominant_freq = argmax(|FFT(R(t))|[1:]) period = 1 / dominant_freq [seconds]
For §90/91 exact correlation, export aligned timeseries from Prometheus and run pandas.Series.corr. The capacity-context estimate compares peak GPU throughput vs L3 bandwidth ceiling; it is not a bottleneck verdict by itself.
HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) is the on-GPU DRAM fabric on A100. Every decode step reads all model weights from HBM — this is the primary decode bottleneck. Values are derived from TPOT + model size since nsys hardware counters were not active in this profile. The timeseries is modulated by GPU utilisation %.
HBM BW data not available
📐 Formula & Metrics Used
📊 DCGM_FI_PROF_DRAM_ACTIVE (Prometheus) + derived from TPOT + model architecture (§F74-F78)
§F74 HBM used (MiB) : DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED (per GPU, DCGM) §F75 HBM free (MiB) : DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE §F76 HBM BW active % : DCGM_FI_PROF_DRAM_ACTIVE × 100 (fraction of cycles HBM is actively transferring) §F77 HBM peak BW (GB/s): 2,000 GB/s (A100 HBM2e specification) Derived HBM Read BW (when DCGM_FI_PROF_DRAM_ACTIVE unavailable): ASSUMPTION: pure steady-state decode (one weight pass per output token). Invalid when TPOT >> ~200 ms (prefill-heavy or long context — see caveat banner above the HBM tiles when this fires). When hbm_used_mb_mean > 0 (measured): bytes_per_gpu = hbm_used × 0.85 (better — captures actual weight footprint under any quantization) Otherwise: bytes_per_gpu = n_params × 2 / n_gpus (assumes FP16 weights) hbm_read_bw = bytes_per_gpu / (tpot_ms / 1000) [GB/s] e.g. FP16 70B / 8 GPUs: 17.5 GB → 17.5 / 0.024s = 729 GB/s HBM Read Txns/s : hbm_read_bw × 10⁹ / 64 [M/s] 64B = A100 HBM2e cache-line size HBM Write BW : hbm_read_bw × 0.12 (empirical: writes ≈12% of reads in decode) HBM Write Txns/s : hbm_write_bw × 10⁹ / 64 [M/s] Min TPOT (BW-limited): model_bytes_per_gpu / HBM_peak × 1000 [ms/tok] TPOT gap factor : observed_tpot / min_tpot (>1 = compute or other overhead)
DCGM_FI_PROF_DRAM_ACTIVE requires DCGM profiling mode enabled. When absent, derivation from TPOT is accurate during pure decode phases (single large request). During batched prefill, TPOT-derived HBM BW overestimates because TPOT includes compute overhead beyond just memory reads.
Derivation: HBM Read BW = model_bytes_per_GPU / TPOT_s = (params × 2B / n_gpus) / (tpot_ms / 1000). Theoretical min TPOT = model_bytes_per_GPU / HBM_peak_BW × 1000 = 0.0 ms/tok. Observed TPOT 0.0 ms → N/A (TPOT not measured). HBM util = HBM_read_BW / 2000 GB/s = 0.0%. Transactions = BW × 10⁹ / 64 bytes (cache-line size).

🟢 System DRAM (CPU-side) Bandwidth & Transactions

📖 What this chart showsHost DRAM read/write bandwidth from AMD uProf PMU (Data Fabric counters) — the L2 memory tier's physical bandwidth.

What you are looking at: A 4-panel chart: (1) DRAM R/W BW timeline (GB/s). (2) Stacked read + write area. (3) Cache-line transaction rate (M/s). (4) DRAM utilisation vs AMD EPYC peak (~460 GB/s 12-ch DDR5).

Why interactive chart is empty: The interactive report looks for `amduprof_pcm_raw.txt`; the collector also writes `amduprof_pcm_raw.csv`. If only the CSV was written, the interactive builder silently returns None while the static report can still parse it. Fix: ensure both files are written, or update the interactive builder to try both extensions.

How to read: High DRAM BW (>100 GB/s) during inference = hicache L2 tier actively staging KV between DRAM and HBM. Low DRAM BW + high NVMe BW = KV goes NVMe→GPU directly (GPUDirect Storage / ICMSP bypass).

For KV$: Sustained 50+ GB/s during decode = DRAM is the active L2 KV staging tier. Near 460 GB/s peak = DRAM is the bottleneck for KV staging.

How to collect: `sudo AMDuProfPcm -r -m memory -a --msr -d 300 -o raw/amduprof_pcm_raw.csv`. AMOprof mirrors/normalizes the raw output for both static and interactive reports.

CPU-side DRAM bandwidth measured by AMD uProf PCM via hardware PMU counters (default (unrecognised CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8259CL CPU @ 2.50GHz) — Data Fabric DRAM controller metrics). Covers: hicache L2 KV pool access, model loader, OS page cache, SGLang runtime. Sampled every 1.2 seconds. Transactions = BW / 64B cache-line.

Identifies sustained host-memory swap activity that can stall inference. A swap storm is a continuous interval where combined pswpin + pswpout rate exceeds 1000 pages/s (≈ 3.9 MiB/s). When detected, correlates with major page faults and quantifies the write-amplification cost on the underlying NVMe device.

📐 Formula & Derivation
📊 vmstat_timeseries.csv · /proc/vmstat (node_exporter Prometheus job) + nvme_driver_timeseries.csv
swap_in_rate = Δ(node_vmstat_pswpin) / Δt [pages/s, 4 KiB pages] swap_out_rate = Δ(node_vmstat_pswpout) / Δt [pages/s] swap_total_rate = swap_in_rate + swap_out_rate storm_active = swap_total_rate >= STORM_THRESHOLD (default: 1000 pg/s) storm_episode = maximal contiguous run of storm_active = True thrashing_pct = 100 × (count(storm_active) / total_samples) majfault_corr = pearsonr( swap_in_rate , Δ(pgmajfault)/Δt ) → r near +1.0 means swap-in directly triggers major page faults (the page being swapped back in was demand-paged → I/O wait) write_amp_ratio = Δ(nvme_wr_ios) / Δ(pswpout) → ratio of NVMe writes hitting the device vs swap-out pages. >1.0 = filesystem journals, metadata updates amplify writes <1.0 = swap I/O is batched (typical for ZSWAP/multi-page swap) swap_used_pct = 100 × (1 - SwapFree/SwapTotal)
Interpretation: A swap storm directly slows inference: every major page fault stalls the GPU memory pinning path while waiting on synchronous swap-in I/O. Triggers: oversubscribed model loader (model + KV + buffers > DRAM), memory-mapped weight files, large hicache L2 footprint, or transient memory spike from concurrent requests. Mitigations: reduce hicache L2 size, enable zswap, increase vm.swappiness=10 (less eager swap), add physical DRAM, or pin SGLang RSS with cgroups.
Verdict: ✅ Healthy — swap activity well below storm threshold.

🚀 Optimisation Recommendations

📖 What this chart showsAuto-generated recommendations ranked by impact and effort, derived from the bottleneck scoring of this specific run.

What you are looking at: Recommendation cards each with: title, impact badge (HIGH/MED/LOW), effort badge, phase badge, and a detailed explanation with the exact command to run.

For the reference run, the top four recommendations are: 1. CHUNKED PREFILL (HIGH impact, LOW effort): `--chunked-prefill-size 4096` in SGLang. Spreads the 33 s TTFT across multiple steps by interleaving prefill chunks with decode, dramatically reducing perceived first-token latency. 2. SPECULATIVE DECODING (MED impact, MED effort): Draft model amortises HBM reads across multiple accepted tokens, improving 2.3 s/tok TPOT. 3. KV QUANTISATION — AWQ/GPTQ 4-bit (HIGH impact, MED effort): Halves HBM pressure and expands KV pool. 4. NUMA BINDING (LOW impact, LOW effort): `numactl --localalloc` eliminates 91 NUMA migrations/s.

For KV$: KV quantisation (item 3) has cascading benefits: smaller per-token footprint → more tokens in HBM → fewer L2/L3 (AI Memory Node / remote storage) evictions → lower NVMe load → reduced TPOT.
